ink-black.$description: Ink Black — Primary text, heading strokes, card borders, filled CTA backgrounds — the sole carrier of visual weight in an otherwise empty palette

paper-cream.$description: Paper Cream — Page canvas, card surfaces, and the default background — warm off-white that distinguishes the brand from clinical SaaS whites

warm-border.$description: Warm Border — Elevated surface, hairline dividers, and card-on-card separation — one shade deeper than the canvas to create structure without contrast

stone-gray.$description: Stone Gray — Secondary body text, muted labels, subtle borders — never used for primary copy

ash-gray.$description: Ash Gray — Tertiary text, helper copy, disabled states — the quietest voice in the type stack

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Text on dark filled CTAs, occasional card surface where higher contrast is needed against the cream canvas

bureauserif.$description: All headlines and display text. Weight 200 is anti-convention — most editorial sites use 300-400 for serif headlines; the extra-light whisper forces the serif to feel like quiet authority rather than declaration. Line-height pinned to 1.0 creates tight, overlapping baselines that read as deliberately set rather than browser-default. Tracking locked at -0.03em across every size, tightening the letterforms into a cohesive display voice.

inter.$description: Body text, nav items, buttons, labels, metadata — the entire non-display UI. A single weight (400) with no bold variant keeps the sans side neutral so the serif can dominate. Tracking is slightly negative on body (-0.011em at 16px) and near-zero on small text, giving Inter a set, editorial feel rather than a default web feel.
